draft.title: Counting principles
card: When choices are made one after another, multiply the number of ways for each step. A meal with 3 mains and then 4 drinks gives 3 × 4 = 12 meals.
When you pick one option from separate groups, and only one choice is made, add the numbers. Choosing one book from 5 novels or 6 atlases gives 5 + 6 = 11 books.
Ask first: do I make one choice after another, or do I pick just one item from different groups?
Some problems use both. Work out each part, then combine them with the right principle.
draft.remember: Steps one after another: multiply. Alternatives: add.

a.q: Priya chooses one of 4 hats and then one of 5 scarves. How many hat and scarf outfits are possible?
a.why: The two choices are made one after another, so multiply: 4 × 5 = 20. Adding gives 9, which would count only a single item from the two groups, not an outfit of both.
a.clue: She picks a hat and then a scarf.

b.q: A café sells 6 hot drinks and 4 cold drinks. Sam buys one drink, then picks one of 3 snacks. How many drink and snack choices are there?
b.why: The drink is one choice from two groups, so add: 6 + 4 = 10 drinks. The snack comes after, so multiply: 10 × 3 = 30. Using 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 wrongly multiplies the two drink groups, which are alternatives.
b.clue: Hot and cold drinks are alternatives. The snack is a second step.
